claims.text: Conventionally synthesized single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys have high saturation magnetization and coercive fields no greater than about 100 Oe.
Post-synthesis annealing at an intermediate temperature can induce atomic-scale chemical ordering in an fcc FeCoNi matrix.
An annealing range of 600–800 °C is suitable for promoting ordering in fcc FeCoNi-based alloys.
Annealing hold time and cooling rate can be optimized to induce long-range or significant short-range order while preserving a single-phase fcc structure.
The ordering-promoting heat treatment can avoid precipitation of secondary phases.
Ordering may produce antiphase boundaries in the fcc FeCoNi matrix.
Atomic chemical ordering increases local magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Atomic ordering and antiphase boundaries provide enhanced pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy raises the energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
A higher energy barrier for domain-wall motion increases the coercive field relative to the chemically disordered counterpart.
The ordering-promoting heat treatment will produce more than an order-of-magnitude increase in coercivity relative to a baseline near 100 Oe.
The heat-treated alloy will maintain a high saturation magnetization while its coercivity increases.
The proposed coercivity enhancement applies only when the alloy remains single-phase fcc after heat treatment.
The proposed effect is expected at room-temperature magnetic measurement conditions.
